title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this first draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic framework for tame or polyhedral-type spaces. There is a class \(\mathcal F\) of 'figures' and a subclass \(\mathcal M\) of 'multiplicités'. Two basic relations are used:
- \(\le\): 'is a sub-figure of'.
- \(\preccurlyeq\) (written \(\lesssim\) in the transcription): roughly 'is a subdivision / refinement of'.

From these he builds a composite relation \(F \ll G\), meaning there is \(G'\) with \(F \le G' \preccurlyeq G\). Grothendieck spells this out on p.83; it reads as 'F is a sub-figure of a subdivision of G', though the direction of \(\preccurlyeq\) is my inference. Axiom C7, used on p.83, is an exchange or commutation law that lets one rewrite a mixed chain. It is what makes \(\ll\) transitive.

This page begins by stating axiom C8(0), a two-sided rigidity condition. The margin, written in large letters, says 'précision !'.
- (a) If \(X \le \Phi \preccurlyeq X\) with \(\Phi \in \mathcal F\) and \(X \in \mathcal M\), then \(X = \Phi\).
- (b) If \(X \preccurlyeq \Psi \le X\), then \(X = \Psi\).
In words: a loop formed by one sub-figure step and one subdivision step must be trivial. This is a 'no proper self-embedding up to subdivision' or Cantor–Bernstein-type rigidity.

He then finishes the proof begun on p.81. There, \(F_X\), \(G_X\) and \(\bar G_X\) are inverse images, induced on the multiplicity \(X\), of the figures in a chain \(F \ll G \ll F\). The argument runs:
1. From \(X \le F_X \preccurlyeq X\), axiom (a) gives \(X = F_X\).
2. Since \(X \le \bar G_X \le F_X = X\), it follows that \(X = \bar G_X\).
3. Then \(\bar G_X = X \preccurlyeq G_X \le X\), so axiom (b) gives \(X = G_X\).
4. In particular \(X \le G_X\), hence \(X \le G\).

Remark: C8 is obviously necessary for \(\ll\) to be an order relation (antisymmetry), and is presumably also sufficient.

Corollary: if \(F \ll G\) and \(G \ll F\), then \(F = G\). Proof sketch: show \(F \le G\) by testing on multiplicities. For every \(X \in \mathcal M\), \(X \le F\) should imply \(X \le G\), which is the criterion of p.80. This test uses the induced chain \(F_X \ll G_X \ll X\), drawn in the diagram at the bottom of the page. The reverse inclusion \(G \le F\) follows by symmetry.

Overall this is order-theoretic axiomatics: making the composite of 'sub-object' and 'refinement' a partial order on figures, as groundwork for a tame-topology foundation.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. The page relies on prior results (p.80 criterion, prop. of p.70, axiom C7) that are not reproduced here.
The 'sufficient' half of the Remark is asserted without proof; the next page (p.83) gives a more direct argument via C7, suggesting he was still reorganizing the proof.

ideas.what: Axiom C8: loops X ≤ Φ ≼ X or X ≼ Ψ ≤ X are trivial (rigidity of sub-figure/subdivision cycles)
ideas.modern_name: antisymmetry condition for a composite of two preorders; Cantor–Bernstein-type rigidity for polyhedra / tame sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology (e.g. invariance of dimension and Euler characteristic arguments); no specific axiomatic source
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only sketches 'topologie modérée' without such axioms

ideas.what: Relation F ≪ G defined as 'sub-figure of a subdivision', proved to be a partial order using C7 (exchange) and C8 (rigidity)
ideas.modern_name: composite relation / span-like order generated by monos and refinements; related to factorization-system-style exchange laws

ideas.what: Testing inclusion F ≤ G on multiplicities X ≤ F via induced (inverse-image) figures F_X, G_X
ideas.modern_name: detecting subobjects by a generating family / pullback-stable subobjects

missed.claim: Grothendieck was building an axiomatic order-theoretic foundation for tame topology. It uses figures, multiplicities, sub-figure and subdivision relations, and axioms C1–C8. This programme was never published or completed, and the axiomatics differ from o-minimality and from Shiota-style tame categories.
missed.quote: Bien sûr, C 8 est nécessaire pour que ≪ soit une relation d'ordre.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical record of how Grothendieck intended to realize the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. Comparison with o-minimal structures and with PL / semi-algebraic category axiomatics could be of historical interest. Mathematically, this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary order-theoretic axiom checking (antisymmetry of a composite relation). Its interest is mainly as evidence of an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology programme, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: The relation symbol written as \lesssim is in the image a curly ≼ (\preccurlyeq), consistent with pp.81 and 83.
The margin note 'précision !' is written diagonally beside a double vertical bar marking C8(0).
'Et c'est ainsi suffisant' is uncertain; it may read 'Et il est aussi suffisant'.
In the corollary header, 'vu prop. ...' is followed by a crossed-out reference (looks like '1 (i) (?)') above the line 'Si F ≪ G et G ≪ F, on a F = G'.
The final diagram reads F ≪ G ≪ F over F_X ≪ G_X ≪ X, with an X below F_X, and with vertical ≥/≤ marks between the rows.
